--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 1.  Relating \(\det H\) and \(\det M\)

Subtract the first row from each of the other rows.  
The resulting matrix is block‑upper–triangular:

\[
\begin{pmatrix}
1 & \mathbf 1^{\!T} \\[2mm]
\mathbf 0 & A-J_n
\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
1 & \mathbf 1^{\!T} \\[2mm]
\mathbf 0 & -2M
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Row–operations of the type “row ← row – row₁” do not change the
determinant, so  

\[
\det H=\det\!\bigl(\,{-2M}\,\bigr)=(-2)^{\,n}\det M .
\]

Hence  

\[
|\det M|=\frac{|\det H|}{2^{\,n}}. \tag{1}
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 2.  Hadamard’s bound for \(H\)

Every row of \(H\) consists of \(\pm1\)’s, so its Euclidean norm is
\(\sqrt{n+1}\).  By Hadamard’s inequality,

\[
|\det H|\le (\,\sqrt{n+1}\,)^{\,n+1}=(n+1)^{\frac{n+1}{2}}.
\]

Combining this with (1) gives the universal bound  

\[
|\det M|\le \frac{(n+1)^{\frac{n+1}{2}}}{2^{\,n}}. \tag{2}
\]

Since \(\det M\) is an integer, the actual maximum is the integer part
of the right–hand side:

\[
\max_{M\in\{0,1\}^{n\times n}} |\det M|
\;\le\;
\Big\lfloor\frac{(n+1)^{\frac{n+1}{2}}}{2^{\,n}}\Big\rfloor .
\tag{3}
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 3.  When is the bound attained?

If there exists a Hadamard matrix of order \(n+1\) (i.e. a \((n+1)\times (n+1)\)
matrix \(H\) with entries \(\pm1\) and pairwise orthogonal rows), then
\(|\det H|=(n+1)^{\frac{n+1}{2}}\).  Writing such an \(H\) in the block
form above yields  

\[
M=\frac{J_n-A}{2}\in\{0,1\}^{n\times n},
\qquad\det M=\frac{|\det H|}{2^{\,n}}
          =\frac{(n+1)^{\frac{n+1}{2}}}{2^{\,n}} .
\]

Hadamard matrices are known to exist for every order \(n+1\) that is a
multiple of \(4\) (and for the trivial cases \(1,2\)).  Consequently,
when  

\[
n+1\equiv 0\pmod4\qquad(\text{i.e. }n\equiv3\pmod4),
\]

the bound (2) is attained.  For the remaining values of \(n\) the
maximum equals the integer part (3).

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 4.  Answer

\[
\boxed{\displaystyle
\max_{M\in\{0,1\}^{n\times n}} |\det M|
   =\Big\lfloor\frac{(n+1)^{\frac{n+1}{2}}}{2^{\,n}}\Big\rfloor }.
\]

Equality holds whenever a Hadamard matrix of order \(n+1\) exists (in
particular for all \(n\equiv3\pmod4\)).  Hence the maximal determinant
of an \(n\times n\) \(0\!-\!1\) matrix is the integer part of
\((n+1)^{(n+1)/2}/2^{\,n}\).<|eot_id|> <|end_of_text|>
